title: Power Abroad, Turmoil at Home
partB: Turner's 1893 argument that the closing of the frontier ended the first period of American history, and that the frontier had made American democracy.
The intercepted 1917 German proposal that Mexico ally itself with Germany and recover Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona.
The consumer practice of taking goods home on a small down payment and paying the rest in scheduled portions, which spread the decade's goods on credit.
The 1904 claim that the United States might intervene in an American nation guilty of chronic wrongdoing, to keep European powers from intervening first.
The 1924 law that fixed immigration quotas by national origin, favoring northern and western Europe and effectively closing the door to Asia.
The cease-fire of November 11, 1918, that stopped the fighting on the Western Front.
Purchasing stock with a small down payment and a broker's loan for the balance, so that gains and losses alike were magnified.
The constitutional ban on the manufacture, sale, and transportation of intoxicating liquor, in force from 1920 to 1933.
